title: Group B Streptococcus: Risk-Based Intrapartum Prophylaxis

evidenceAudit.scope: Woman in labour at risk of early-onset neonatal group B streptococcal (GBS) disease: indications for intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP), antibiotic doses and timing, and neonatal observation, using one hospital guideline and one antimicrobial page. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.

pathophysiology.summary: Early-onset GBS disease in the newborn is linked to maternal GBS carriage, so IAP is given in labour to women at risk. Antibiotics should start as soon as possible after the onset of labour and the first dose at least 4 hours before delivery for best effect. GBS bacteriuria in pregnancy needs treatment at diagnosis as well as IAP in labour. A planned caesarean section with intact membranes and no labour does not need GBS-specific prophylaxis.

clinicalManagement.title: Identify indication
actions: Check for previous GBS disease in a baby, bacteriuria, carriage, preterm labour or fever.

clinicalManagement.title: Give IAP
clinicalManagement.timeframe: As soon as possible after labour starts
actions: Benzylpenicillin 3 g intravenously then 1.5 g every 4 hours until delivery.
Non-severe penicillin allergy: cefuroxime 1.5 g then 750 mg every 8 hours. Severe allergy: vancomycin 1 g every 12 hours (Southern Trust) or teicoplanin per the Forth Valley page.

clinicalManagement.title: Prelabour rupture of membranes at term
actions: Known carrier: immediate IAP and induction as soon as reasonably possible.
Negative or unknown status: offer induction after 24 hours.

clinicalManagement.title: Neonatal observation
actions: Adequate IAP and well: no special observation.
Inadequate IAP: vital signs at 0, 1 and 2 hours then 2-hourly until 12 hours; encourage breastfeeding.

regimens.indication: Intrapartum prophylaxis for early-onset GBS disease (first line)
regimens.patientGroup: Women in labour with an indication for IAP and no penicillin allergy
regimens.frequency: Loading dose as soon as possible after labour starts, then every 4 hours
adjustments: No renal adjustment is given in the sources opened.
First dose at least 4 hours before delivery to optimise efficacy.
monitoring: Record time of first dose relative to delivery.
contraindications: Penicillin allergy: use cefuroxime or, if severe, vancomycin or teicoplanin.

teaching.scope: Woman in labour at risk of early-onset neonatal group B streptococcal (GBS) disease: indications for intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis (IAP), antibiotic doses and timing, and neonatal observation, using one hospital guideline and one antimicrobial page.
learningObjectives: Offer IAP for the listed risk factors.
Start as soon as possible after labour begins and at least 4 hours before delivery.
pitfalls: Giving the first dose too late.
keyPoints: Planned caesarean without labour does not need GBS-specific IAP.
Fever of 38 degrees Celsius or more needs broad-spectrum cover.
